analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and file metadata against the canonical index and selected T-041 detail. ClusterConfiguration.swift:168–176 replaces blanket exclusion of resident tensor assistants from coordinator-paired setups with exact equality to this build's artifact-specific public policy. Runtime/model, tensor-mode, serial-prefill and private-image restrictions remain. This expands public-serving eligibility but does not, in the supplied code, bypass authorization.
ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts+Release.swift:54 and ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts.swift:263 (head patch) switch default declarations from declared to current. The latter's head patch at 296–302 selects an artifact/runtime-specific assistant and includes it in resourcePolicySHA256. Release generation still filters consistent passing model records, matches artifact hashes and refuses description failures or empty results. Existing description logic checks worker/build/artifact pins; parity qualification construction is unchanged. No encryption, token handling, billing or SSD-cache behavior changes are visible; T-041 mitigations are not directly altered here.
No concrete regression is established within this scope. Integration must examine ClusterPublicModels.current and tensorAssistant, assistant qualification evidence, and DistributedInstalledNativeStart.resourcePolicySHA256/start validation. Confirm release facts and both installed members use the same declaration, bind the actual assistant policy to admission, and only publish parity claims supported for speculative execution. These are material unresolved contracts for T-007, T-027, T-052, T-054 and T-056, plus A-017/A-018 resource and qualification assumptions; comments alone do not establish them. Unchanged authorization callers and native assistant implementation were not supplied, and ClusterConfiguration's base source is available only through bounded change context.
